abstract: Murine parietal yolk sac carcinoma cells were examined by scanning and transmission electron microscopy to determine the ultrastructural changes resulting from growth, in vitro, in media containing different serum concentrations. Cells grown in medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) formed spherical bodies, were gradually oval with numerous surface microvilli, well-organized microtubules, abundant free polysomes and a well-developed Golgi apparatus. By contrast, cells grown in 1% FBS failed to form multicellular spheres, were generally flattened over the growth surface and lacked the surface and intracellular features demonstrated when cells were grown in 10% serum. These differences could explain the alterations in the glycosylation of secreted glycoprotein associated with culture in the presence of low serum.
abstract_ja: マウス卵黄嚢癌細胞を、10%および1%のウシ胎児血清を含む培地で培養し、その超微細構造変化を走査型および透過型電子顕微鏡で観察した。10%血清で培養した細胞は球状の集塊を形成し、楕円形で表面に多数の微絨毛を持ち、微小管が整然と配列し、遊離ポリソームに富み、ゴルジ装置がよく発達していた。一方、1%血清で培養した細胞は多細胞性の球体を形成できず、基質上で扁平に広がり、これらの表面および細胞内の特徴を欠いていた。これらの超微細構造の違いは、低血清条件下で分泌糖タンパク質の糖鎖形成が変化する原因を説明しうる。
